questions.q: What is the Ports tab for?
questions.explain: Each UART gets a role; without it the FC doesn't know where to look for the receiver or GPS.

questions.q: Serial RX is enabled on UART2, the receiver is soldered to UART1. The result?
options: Arming is impossible because of RXLOSS
The FC listens to the wrong port
questions.explain: The port role must match the physical connection.

questions.q: Can you assign two devices to one UART?
options: Only GPS and VTX on F7
questions.explain: A UART is one TX/RX pair. Two roles on one port conflict.
Software emulation of a UART on regular pins: it helps when you've run out of UARTs, but it's no good for SBUS.

questions.q: The FC's USB port is shown in Ports as…
questions.explain: USB VCP is a virtual COM port for the configurator and the CLI.

questions.q: How many ports with MSP are allowed at the same time?
options: Any number, if the baud rates differ
questions.explain: A fourth one causes the MSP settings to reset.

questions.q: An ExpressLRS receiver is connected to UART2. The aircraft doesn't see the sticks. The cause is in this diff:
questions.fragment:
serial 1 64 115200 57600 0 115200
set serialrx_provider = SBUS
set serialrx_inverted = OFF
options: serialrx_provider = SBUS, but ELRS speaks CRSF — you need serialrx_provider = CRSF
Mask 64 on UART2 means MSP, not Serial RX — the receiver is connected to the telemetry port
115200 baud is too low for ELRS: CRSF requires 420000, and that is set in the serial command
serialrx_inverted = OFF: ELRS on UART2 needs the software inverter turned on
questions.explain: serial 1 (UART2) with mask 64 is Serial RX, that's correct; the protocol is wrong.
